questions.question: What access modifier makes members accessible only within the same class?
questions.explanation: Private members are restricted to the class where they are defined.

questions.question: What access modifier makes members accessible from anywhere?
questions.explanation: Public members can be accessed from any part of the program.

questions.question: What access modifier allows access within the class and its subclasses?
questions.explanation: Protected members are accessible in the class and its derived classes.

questions.question: What methods provide controlled access to private data?
questions.explanation: Getters and setters allow controlled reading and writing of private attributes.

questions.question: What principle bundles data and methods together?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation wraps data and methods into a single unit.

questions.question: What is the practice of hiding internal implementation details called?
questions.explanation: Information hiding restricts direct access to object internals.

questions.question: What type of method only retrieves but doesn't modify data?
questions.explanation: Getters return the value of private attributes without changing them.

questions.question: What type of method modifies private data?
questions.explanation: Setters assign new values to private attributes with validation.

questions.question: What naming convention indicates a private member in Python?
questions.explanation: Double underscore prefix triggers name mangling for privacy in Python.

questions.question: What benefit does encapsulation provide?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation protects data from unauthorized access and modification.

questions.question: Which access level in Java allows access only within the same package?
questions.explanation: Members with no modifier have package-private (default) access in Java.

questions.question: What does a well-written setter method typically do before assigning a value?
questions.explanation: Setters commonly validate input to keep the object's state consistent.

questions.question: In C#, which feature provides get and set accessors concisely?
questions.explanation: C# properties wrap fields with get/set accessor syntax.

questions.question: Which Python decorator turns a method into an attribute-like read accessor?
questions.explanation: The @property decorator lets a method be accessed like an attribute.

questions.question: A getter method is also known as what?
questions.explanation: Getters are accessors because they provide read access to data.

questions.question: A setter method is also known as what?
questions.explanation: Setters are mutators because they modify the object's state.

questions.question: Which access modifier is the most restrictive in Java?
questions.explanation: Private is the most restrictive, allowing access only inside the class.

questions.question: Which is a recommended way to make a class immutable?
options: Make fields final and provide no setters
Store fields in a public array
questions.explanation: Final fields without setters prevent state changes after construction.

questions.question: What Java keyword prevents a field from being reassigned after initialization?
questions.explanation: Final fields must be assigned once and cannot be modified afterwards.

questions.question: In Python, what does a single leading underscore on an attribute name indicate?
questions.explanation: A single underscore is a naming convention signaling internal use; it is not enforced.

questions.question: What does Python's name mangling turn __secret into inside class Foo?
questions.explanation: Name mangling rewrites __name as _ClassName__name to reduce accidental access.

questions.question: Which C++ keyword grants a function or class access to private members?
questions.explanation: The friend keyword lets specific external functions or classes access private members.

questions.question: A BankAccount class hides its balance field and exposes only deposit() and withdraw(). Which principle is applied?
questions.explanation: Hiding the balance and controlling access through methods is encapsulation.

questions.question: Why should fields generally be declared private?
options: It makes the code run faster
It prevents uncontrolled modification of state
It is required by the compiler
questions.explanation: Private fields stop outside code from corrupting the object's state.

questions.question: What is the default access specifier for members of a C++ class?
questions.explanation: C++ class members are private by default; struct members are public by default.

questions.question: What is the term for exposing internal representation details that should have stayed hidden?
questions.explanation: A leaky abstraction exposes implementation details, weakening encapsulation.
